full_judgment:
4. Defendant Nos. 1-5 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement contending that the power of attorney and all the deeds executed on the basis of the said power of attorney are forged, fraudulent, without consideration and void and as such the plaintiff has acquired no title and interest in the suit land. The defendants contended that the suit land is a homestead plot which Jaladhar Gope and Adhari Gope used to hold along with other lands. Defendants denied that Santosh was a son of Balaram. They contended that Jaladhar died leaving not only 3 sons but also a daughter Madhumala Gope. Madhumala's son was Santosh. Santosh used to reside in his maternal uncle's house situated in the suit land. In 1356 B.S. Jagadish, Sidam, Basana and Haridasi gave korfa settlement of the suit land and other lands to Santosh and delivered possession of the same and thereafter they left for Assam. While Santosh was possessing the suit homestead land by residing therein with his family and by cultivating other pattan lands through bargadars Jagadish and Sidam again came to this country from Assam and they sold away their balance land after the pattan to Kiamuddin and others by a registered deed of sale Ext. A dated 22.12.55 Jagadish was an illiterate man and Sidam knew how to write. In this deed date 22.12.55 Jaladhar had put his left thumb impression and Sidam put his signature. On 18th Bhadra, 1376 B.S. corresponding to 4.9.69 Santosh sold away the suit homestead land to Afazuddin Pramanik (Ext. A) the predecessor of these defendants. Santosh also sold away his other land by other kabalas to Faizuddin and others (Ext. A(1) and A(2). Thus Afajuddin possessing the suit homestead plot within the knowledge of the plaintiff died leaving behind the contesting defendants as his heirs. 

 9. The learned Subordinate Judge then quoted from the judgment in the Criminal Case Ext. G and found that the alleged loss of the power of attorney gives rise to a suspicion. He also found from Exts. 6,7,8,8(a), 9,10,10(a) and Exts D.E. and F that Santosh had been admitted to be the nephew of Jagadish and Balaram and not the son of Balaram. Next the learned Subordinate Judge found that the elder brother of the plaintiff paid rent for 1.09 acres of land in India on 7.12.60. If he had exchanged the land in 1963 then the original receipt of payment of rent in 1960 could not be retained by him. The learned Subordinate Judge then took into consideration the affidavit Ext. D sworn by Jagadish Gope and found that this is an admissible document, In this affidavit Jagadish Gope stated that no power of attorney was executed by him and his brothers and no deed of exchange was executed and registered by virtue of that power of attorney. The learned Subordinate Judge relied on Ext. D and held that the power of attorney was a fake and fraudulent document. He then considered the dakhilas Ext. B series showing korfa pattan of the suit land and other lands by Santosh and the dakhilas showing payment of rent by Santosh. He also found that Santosh filed case against his bargaders in respect of the suit land and Ext. A series show that Santosh sold away the suit land and other lands to various pruchasers including the predecessor-in-interest of the defendants Afazuddin. With regard to possession the learned Subordinate Judge did not discuss the evidence of P.Ws. at all but held that the possession is that of the contesting defendants as bargader of Santosh and found that the story of dispossession of the plaintiff is not true. He, therefore, dismissed the suit. 

 23. With regard to the learned Subordinate Judge's finding regarding the title and possession of the defendants Mr. Shafique Ahmed submits that the learned Subordinate Judge has completely misread and has also failed to take into consideration important evidence on record Exts. B-B (6) are the dakhilas showing the taking of korfa pattan of the suit land and other lands by Santosh in these dakhilas Ext. B(4), Ext. B(5) and Ext. B(6) Santosh Kumar Gope is shown as the tenant. The learned Subordinate Judge has not explained as to how an under-tenancy can be created when there is no endorsement by the tenants themselves. Further it does not appear from the remaining dakhilas that Santosh Kumar Gope was given any transferable interest in the tenancy. Mr. Shafique Ahmed has further drawn my attention to the deeds of sale Ext. A series by which the predecessor-in-interest of the defendants alleged to have purchased the suit land from Santosh. The seller is described in all these documents as Santosh Kumar Ghosh, son of late Surendra Kumar Ghosh and there is no explanation that Santosh Kumar Ghosh is the same man as Santosh Kumar Gope. The learned Subordinate Judge has held that the possession of the defendants was the possession on the basis of being bargaders of Santosh. Mr. Shafique Ahmed submits that this is a misreading of evidence because defendant No. 1 has stated in Ext. 10 that he was not a bargader of Santosh but a bargader of the elder brother of the plaintiff. He has also drawn my attention to the non-consideration of Ext. 2(a) which shows that on 16.1.56 Jagadish and others gave a khai Khalashi bandabasta of the suit land to D.W.5 Sk. Jurman Ali for 2 years. Mr. Shafique Ahmed Submits that had the learned Subordinate Judge considered Ext.2(a) he could not have come to the conclusion that the suit land was settled with Santosh in korafa tenancy in 1356 B.S. because the suit land was given in khai Khalashi bandabasta to P.W 5 subsequently in 1362 B.S. by the same persons.
